blocks.md: This lesson follows **Locating a Divergence** in *Durable Execution* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Durable Execution, § Locating a Divergence
blocks.md: When an automated software-repair workflow undergoes regression replay, execution proceeds uneventfully until reaching the recorded targeted-test result for candidate patch `r18`. The stored test result itself remains identical, but a revised harness assembles a subtly different observation context for the subsequent model call. Waiting until the final repair verdict to compare the runs obscures this earlier discrepancy under layers of compounding tool calls and token generations. Effective debugging requires pinpointing the exact architectural boundary where two executions first cease to agree within the recorded evidence.

questions.q: The section **Locating a Divergence** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: An acknowledgment is durable only against the faults its storage tier survives, so each write's durability is declared against a failure domain rather than assumed.

A sampled model reply cannot be regenerated, so reproduction substitutes recorded inputs at nondeterministic boundaries, and one recording serves time-travel inspection, harness regression, and counterfactual branching.
Debugging two executions steps boundary by boundary from a verified checkpoint to the first mismatch under a declared equivalence, because every later difference may be a consequence.
An admitted operation whose effect cannot be proven present or absent is in doubt and must be reconciled before any re-dispatch, the recovery-side view of an uncertain outcome.
